question.text: What is a memory leak and how do you prevent it in C?
expected_concepts: memory no longer accessible but not released
Leaked memory is lost until program terminates
memory leak = allocated memory no longer reachable but not freed
common_mistakes: Confusing memory leak with dangling pointer
Saying OS automatically prevents all leaks
Thinking leaks only matter in short programs
frees in success path but not error path — leak on error exit
assumes OS reclaims memory during run — it does only at process termination
question.reference_answer: A memory leak occurs when dynamically allocated memory (using malloc/calloc) is not released using free() after use, causing that memory to remain occupied and unavailable for reuse.
possible_followups: Valgrind detects leaks by tracking all allocations and checking freeing at exit
leaks in long-running programs cause gradual memory exhaustion
set pointer to NULL after free — does not prevent leak but prevents double free
RAII pattern (common in C++) avoids leaks by tying lifetime to scope
every malloc/calloc must have a corresponding free on all code paths
